translations.idiomatic: After driving out Jing, when Changchao was dismissed Xia Song was summoned from Beijing as chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣先論竦在幷州杖殺私僕，復與諫官、御史言竦論議與陳執中異，不可共事。

translations.literal: Dingchen had earlier argued that in Bing Prefecture Song beat a private servant to death; he again spoke with remonstrators and censors that Song's views differed from Chen Zhizhong's and they could not serve together.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen had earlier argued that in Bing Prefecture Song beat a private servant to death; he again spoke with remonstrators and censors that Song's views differed from Chen Zhizhong's and they could not serve together.

sentences.zh: 竦既罷，遂以刑部員外郎知諫院。

translations.literal: When Song was dismissed he was then made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments managing the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Song was dismissed Dingchen was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments managing the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上言：「朝廷方與契丹保誓約，而楊懷敏增廣塘水，輒生事，民或怨叛，雖斬懷敏，無及矣。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The court is now keeping the oath with the Khitan, yet Yang Huaimin enlarged the pond water and rashly created trouble—the people may rebel in resentment; though Huaimin be executed it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "The court keeps the oath with the Khitan, yet Yang Huaimin enlarged pond water and rashly created trouble—the people may rebel; though Huaimin be executed it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 遂為河北體量安撫，令經度塘水利害，而鼎臣更顧望，依違不能決。

translations.literal: He was then made Hebei Pacification and Comfort Commissioner to measure pond water benefits and harms, yet Dingchen looked back and forth and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hebei Pacification Commissioner to measure pond benefits and harms, yet Dingchen hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 昌朝與都轉運使施昌言議河事不合，鼎臣自度支副使拜天章閣待制，代昌言，數月卒。

translations.literal: Changchao and Circuit Transport Commissioner Shi Changyan disagreed on river affairs; Dingchen was promoted from Vice Fiscal Commissioner to Hanlin Attendant of the Heavenly Writings Hall in Changyan's place and died within months.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao and Transport Commissioner Shi Changyan disagreed on river affairs; Dingchen was promoted from Vice Fiscal Commissioner to Hanlin Attendant in Changyan's place and died within months.

sentences.zh: 呂景初

translations.literal: Lu Jingchu
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingchu

sentences.zh: 呂景初，字沖之，開封酸棗人。

translations.literal: Lu Jingchu, courtesy name Chongzhi, was a native of Suanzao in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingchu, whose courtesy name was Chongzhi, came from Suanzao in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭試秘書省校書郎，舉進士，歷汝州推官，改著作佐郎、知夏陽縣，僉書河南府判官，通判幷州。

translations.literal: By his father's privilege he tested as collator of the Secretariat, passed the jinshi, served as judicial officer of Ru Prefecture, was changed to Editorial Assistant and governed Xiayang County, signed as adjudicator of Henan Prefecture, and vice-prefect of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By his father's privilege he tested as Secretariat collator, passed the jinshi, served as judicial officer of Ru Prefecture, became Editorial Assistant governing Xiayang County, signed as Henan adjudicator, and vice-prefect of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高若訥薦為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Gao Ruone recommended him as Attending Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruone recommended him as Attending Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃薨，有司請依荊王故事，輟視朝五日，或欲更增日，聽上裁，乃增至七日。

translations.literal: When Honored Consort Zhang died the offices asked to follow the Prince of Jing precedent and halt court audience for five days; some wished more days at the emperor's discretion—it was increased to seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Consort Zhang died the offices asked to follow the Prince of Jing precedent and halt audience five days; some wished more at imperial discretion—it reached seven.

sentences.zh: 景初言：「妃一品當輟朝三日，禮官希旨，使恩禮過荊王，不可以示天下。」

translations.literal: Jingchu said: "A consort of first rank should halt audience three days; ritual officers curried favor and made favor exceed the Prince of Jing—this cannot be shown to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu said, "A consort of first rank should halt audience three days; ritual officers curried favor and made favor exceed the Prince of Jing—this cannot be shown the realm."

sentences.zh: 妃既追冊為皇后，又詔立忌，景初力爭，乃罷。

translations.literal: After the consort was posthumously enfeoffed as empress an edict also established a memorial day; Jingchu argued forcefully and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After she was posthumously enfeoffed as empress an edict established a memorial day; Jingchu argued forcefully and it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 時兵冗，用度乏，景初奏疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time troops were redundant and expenditures lacking; Jingchu memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Troops were redundant and expenditures lacking; Jingchu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「聖人在上，不能無災，而有救災之術。

translations.literal: "When a sage is above, there cannot be no disaster, yet there is art to relieve disaster.
translations.idiomatic: "When a sage reigns, disaster cannot be absent, yet there is art to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 今百姓困窮，國用虛竭，利源已盡，惟有減用度爾。

translations.literal: Now the people are impoverished and state use empty—the sources of profit are exhausted; only reducing expenditures remains.
translations.idiomatic: The people are impoverished and state use empty—profit sources are exhausted; only reducing expenditures remains.

sentences.zh: 用度之廣，無如養兵。

translations.literal: Of expenditures none is so broad as maintaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: No expenditure is so broad as maintaining troops.

sentences.zh: 比年招置太多，未加揀汰。

translations.literal: In recent years recruitment was too great without selection and pruning.
translations.idiomatic: Recent recruitment was too great without selection.

sentences.zh: 若兵皆勇健，能捍寇敵，竭民膏血以啖之，猶為不可，況羸疾老怯者，又常過半，徒費粟帛，戰則先奔，致勇者亦相牽以敗。

translations.literal: If troops were all brave and healthy and could repel invaders, draining the people's fat and blood to feed them would still be wrong—how much more when the weak, ill, and cowardly often exceed half, wasting grain and silk, fleeing first in battle and dragging the brave to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If troops were brave and could repel invaders, draining the people to feed them would still be wrong—how much more when the weak and cowardly exceed half, wasting grain, fleeing first and dragging the brave to defeat.

sentences.zh: 當祖宗時，四方割據，中國才百餘州，民力未完，耕植未廣，然用度充足者，兵少故也，而所征皆克。

translations.literal: In the time of the founding emperors the realm was divided and China had only a bit more than a hundred prefectures; the people's strength was not complete and farming not broad—yet expenditures were sufficient because troops were few, and what was attacked was always taken.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperors the realm was divided and China had barely a hundred prefectures; strength was incomplete and farming not broad—yet expenditures sufficed because troops were few, and campaigns succeeded.

sentences.zh: 自數十年來，用數倍之兵，所向必敗。

translations.literal: For several decades we have used several times the troops and wherever we go we are defeated.
translations.idiomatic: For decades we have used several times the troops and wherever we go we are defeated.

sentences.zh: 以此，知兵在精，不在眾也。

translations.literal: From this one knows troops lie in quality, not multitude.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows troops lie in quality, not multitude.

sentences.zh: 議者屢以為言，陛下不即更者，由大臣偷安避怨，論事之臣，又復緘默，則此弊何時而息。

translations.literal: Discussants have repeatedly spoken yet Your Majesty has not immediately changed because great ministers steal ease and avoid resentment and those who discuss affairs again keep silent—when will this harm cease?
translations.idiomatic: Discussants have spoken yet Your Majesty has not changed because ministers steal ease and avoid resentment and discussants keep silent—when will this harm cease?

sentences.zh: 望詔中書、樞密院，議罷招補，而汰冗濫。」

translations.literal: I wish an edict to the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to deliberate ending recruitment and pruning redundancy."
translations.idiomatic: I wish an edict to the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to end recruitment and prune redundancy."

sentences.zh: 又言：「坐而論道者，三公也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who sit and discuss the Way are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Those who sit and discuss the Way are the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 今輔臣奏事，非留身求罷免，未嘗從容獨見，以評講治道。

translations.literal: Now assisting ministers memorialize affairs; unless they stay behind seeking dismissal they never meet alone at ease to discuss governing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now assisting ministers memorialize; unless seeking dismissal they never meet alone to discuss governing the Way.

sentences.zh: 雖願治如堯、舜，得賢如稷、契，而未至於治者，抑由此也。

translations.literal: Though one wishes to govern like Yao and Shun and gain the worthy like Ji and Qi, one has not reached governance—perhaps this restrains it.
translations.idiomatic: Though one wishes to govern like Yao and Shun and gain men like Ji and Qi, one has not reached governance—perhaps this restrains it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下於輔臣、侍從、臺諫之列，擇其忠信通治道者，屢詔而數訪之，幸甚！」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty among assisting ministers, attendants, and remonstrance and censor ranks would choose those loyal, trustworthy, penetrating, and governing the Way, repeatedly edict and frequently inquire—greatly fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty among ministers, attendants, and remonstrance and censor ranks would choose the loyal and penetrating, repeatedly edict and inquire—greatly fortunate!"

sentences.zh: 又與言事御史馬遵、吳中復奏彈梁適與劉宗孟連姻，而宗孟與冀州富人共商販，下開封府劾治，所言不實，皆坐謫，景初通判江寧府。

translations.literal: He also with Remonstrance Officer Ma Zun and Wu Zhongfu memorialized impeaching Liang Shi for marrying Liu Zongmeng and Zongmeng trading with a rich man of Ji Prefecture; Kaifeng investigated and the words were not true—all were punished and demoted; Jingchu was transferred as vice-prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With Remonstrance Officer Ma Zun and Wu Zhongfu he impeached Liang Shi for marrying Liu Zongmeng, who traded with a Ji Prefecture rich man; Kaifeng found the charge false—all were demoted; Jingchu was vice-prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 徙知衡州，復召還臺。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern Heng Prefecture, he was again summoned to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Heng Prefecture, he was again summoned to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，大雨水，景初曰：「此陰盛陽微之誡也。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou great rain came; Jingchu said: "This is the warning of yin flourishing and yang slight."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou's first year great rains came; Jingchu said, "This warns that yin flourishes and yang is slight."

sentences.zh: 乃上疏稱：「商、周之盛，並建同姓；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the flourishing of Shang and Zhou, same-surname kin were all established;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In Shang and Zhou's flourishing, same-surname kin were all established;

sentences.zh: 兩漢皇子，多封大國；

translations.literal: Han imperial sons were often enfeoffed in great states;
translations.idiomatic: Han imperial sons were often enfeoffed in great states;

sentences.zh: 有唐宗室，出為刺史；

translations.literal: Tang clansmen went out as prefects;
translations.idiomatic: Tang clansmen served as prefects;

sentences.zh: 國朝二宗，相繼尹京。

translations.literal: our dynasty's two founders successively governed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: our dynasty's two founders successively governed the capital.

sentences.zh: 是欲本支盛強，有磐石之安，則奸雄不敢內窺，而天下有所倚望矣。

translations.literal: The intent was to make the root branches flourish strong with bedrock security so treacherous heroes dare not spy within and the realm has something to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was flourishing root branches with bedrock security so traitors dare not spy within and the realm has something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 願擇宗子之賢者，使得問安侍膳於宮中，以消奸萌，或尹京典郡，為夾輔之勢。」

translations.literal: I wish to choose worthy clansmen to attend the palace for inquiry and meals to dissolve wicked sprouts, or govern the capital and prefectures as supporting strength."
translations.idiomatic: Choose worthy clansmen to attend the palace for meals to dissolve wicked sprouts, or govern capital and prefectures as supporting strength."

sentences.zh: 時狄青為樞密使，得士卒心，議者憂其為變。

translations.literal: At the time Di Qing was Bureau Commissioner and won soldiers' hearts; discussants worried he would change.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing was Bureau Commissioner and won soldiers' hearts; discussants feared change.

sentences.zh: 景初奏疏曰：「天象謫見，妖人訛言，權臣有虛聲，為兵眾所附，中外為之恟恟。

translations.literal: Jingchu memorialized: "Heaven's image reproves and false men spread rumors; a powerful minister has empty reputation and is attached to by the multitude—inside and outside are alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu memorialized, "Heaven reproves and false men spread rumors; a powerful minister has empty reputation and troops attach to him—inside and outside are alarmed.

sentences.zh: 此機會之際，間不容發，蓋以未立皇子，社稷有此大憂。

translations.literal: At this juncture the interval does not permit hair's breadth—probably because the heir is not yet established and the altars have this great worry.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture no moment permits delay—probably because no heir is established and the altars have this great worry.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下蚤為之計，則人心不搖，國本固矣。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty acts early will hearts not shake and the root be firm."
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty acts early will hearts not shake and the root be firm."

sentences.zh: 數詣中書白執政，請出青。

translations.literal: He several times went to the Secretariat to tell those in power to send Qing out.
translations.idiomatic: He several times told those in power at the Secretariat to send Qing out.

sentences.zh: 文彥博以青忠謹有素，外言皆小人為之，不足置意。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo said Qing was loyal and careful by nature and outside talk was all petty men's doing—not worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo said Qing was loyal by nature and outside talk was petty men's doing—not worth minding.

sentences.zh: 景初曰：「青雖忠，如眾心何，蓋為小人無識，則或以致變。

translations.literal: Jingchu said: "Though Qing is loyal, what of the multitude's heart? If petty men are unwise, change may thereby arise.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu said, "Though Qing is loyal, what of the multitude's heart? Unwise petty men may bring change.

sentences.zh: 大臣宜為朝廷慮，毋牽閭里恩也。」

translations.literal: Great ministers should worry for the court and not be drawn by neighborhood favor."
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers should worry for the court, not neighborhood favor."

sentences.zh: 知制誥劉敞亦論之甚力，卒出青知陳州。

translations.literal: Drafting Gentleman Liu Chang also argued forcefully; in the end Qing was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Gentleman Liu Chang argued forcefully; Qing was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李仲昌以河事敗，內遣中人置獄。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchang failed in river affairs and inner envoys were sent to set up imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchang failed in river affairs and inner envoys set up imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 景初意賈昌朝為之，即言：「事無根原，不出政府，恐陰邪用此，以中傷善良。」

translations.literal: Jingchu thought Jia Changchao was behind it and said: "The affair has no root and does not come from government—I fear hidden evil uses this to strike good men."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu thought Jia Changchao was behind it and said, "The affair has no root outside government—I fear hidden evil strikes good men."

sentences.zh: 乃更遣御史同訊。

translations.literal: Censors were again sent to investigate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were again sent to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 遷右司諫，安撫河北。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer, he pacified Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Officer, he pacified Hebei.

sentences.zh: 還，奏比部員外郎鄭平占籍真定，有田七百餘頃，因請均其徭役，著限田令。

translations.literal: On return he memorialized that Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue Zheng Ping registered household in Zhending with more than seven hundred qing of fields and asked to equalize corvée and establish limited-field law.
translations.idiomatic: On return he memorialized that Zheng Ping registered household in Zhending with seven hundred-plus qing and asked to equalize corvée and establish limited-field law.

sentences.zh: 以戶部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，判都水監，改度支副使，遷吏部員外郎，擢天章閣待制、知諫院，以病，未入謝而卒。

translations.literal: As Outer Gentleman of the Household Ministry concurrently Attending Censor with supervisory duties he adjudicated the Metropolitan Waterworks, was changed to Vice Fiscal Commissioner, transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Hanlin Attendant of the Heavenly Writings Hall managing the Remonstrance Bureau; he was ill and died before entering to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: As Outer Gentleman of the Household Ministry with supervisory censor duties he adjudicated Metropolitan Waterworks, became Vice Fiscal Commissioner, Outer Gentleman of Personnel, Hanlin Attendant managing Remonstrance Bureau; ill, he died before giving thanks.

sentences.zh: 馬遵

translations.literal: Ma Zun
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zun

translations.literal: 〈Attached〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Attached〉

sentences.zh: 馬遵者，字仲塗，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Ma Zun, courtesy name Zhongtu, was a native of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zun, whose courtesy name was Zhongtu, came from Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗以監察御史為江淮發運判官，就遷殿中侍御史為副使。

translations.literal: He once served as Investigating Censor and Jianghuai Transport Vice Commissioner and was promoted on the spot to Attending Palace Censor as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Investigating Censor and Jianghuai Transport Vice Commissioner and was promoted on the spot to Attending Palace Censor as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為言事御史，謫知宣州，後復為右司諫，以禮部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，改吏部，直龍圖閣，卒。

translations.literal: He entered as remonstrance officer, was demoted to govern Xuan Prefecture, later again Right Remonstrance Officer, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites with supervisory censor duties, changed to the Ministry of Personnel, Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as remonstrance officer, was demoted to Xuan Prefecture, later Right Remonstrance Officer, Outer Gentleman of Rites with supervisory censor duties, Ministry of Personnel, Dragon Diagram Attendant, and died.

sentences.zh: 性樂易，善議論，其言事不為激訐，故多見推行，杜衍、范仲淹皆稱道之。

translations.literal: His nature was easy and he was good at discussion; in speaking on affairs he was not harsh and therefore was often carried out—Du Yan and Fan Zhongyan all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Easy by nature and good at discussion, he was not harsh in remonstrance and was often heeded—Du Yan and Fan Zhongyan praised him.

sentences.zh: 吳及，字幾道，通州靜海人。

translations.literal: Wu Ji, courtesy name Jidao, was a native of Jinghai in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji, whose courtesy name was Jidao, came from Jinghai in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十七，以進士起家，為侯官尉。

translations.literal: At seventeen he passed the jinshi and began as Houguan county lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he passed the jinshi and began as Houguan county lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 閩俗多自毒死以誣仇家，官司莫能辨，及悉為讞正，前後活五十三人，提點刑獄移其法於一路。

translations.literal: Min custom often self-poisoned to frame enemy families; officials could not distinguish; Ji fully corrected verdicts—fifty-three lives saved before and after—and the judicial intendant spread his method through the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Min custom often used self-poisoning to frame enemies; officials could not tell; Ji corrected verdicts and saved fifty-three lives; the judicial intendant spread his method through the circuit.

sentences.zh: 辟大理寺檢法官，徙審刑院詳議，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was recruited as examining judge of the Court of Judicial Review, moved to detailed deliberation at the Court of Punishment, and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited as Court of Judicial Review examining judge, he moved to Court of Punishment deliberation and rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是時，仁宗春秋既高，無子，及因推言閹寺，以及繼嗣事。

translations.literal: At the time Renzong's years were already high and he had no son; Ji therefore extended speech on eunuchs and the matter of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's years were high and he had no son; Ji therefore spoke on eunuchs and succession.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe he memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe's first year he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞『官師相規，工執藝事以諫。』

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard 'officials and teachers admonish each other; craftsmen hold their craft to remonstrate.'
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard 'officials and teachers admonish each other; craftsmen remonstrate with their craft.'

sentences.zh: 臣幸得待罪法吏，輒原刑法之本，以效愚忠。

translations.literal: Your servant is fortunate to await punishment as a law officer and ventures the root of penal law to offer loyal foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to serve as a law officer, I venture the root of penal law to offer loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 切惟前世肉刑之設，斷支體，刻肌膚，使終身不息。

translations.literal: I consider that the flesh punishments of former ages cut limbs and carved flesh so suffering never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Former flesh punishments cut limbs and carved flesh so suffering never ceased.

sentences.zh: 漢文感緹縈之言，易之鞭箠，然已死而笞未止，外有輕刑之意，其實殺人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han was moved by Ti Ying's words and changed to flogging, yet those already dead were still flogged—outwardly light punishment, inwardly killing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was moved by Ti Ying and changed to flogging, yet the dead were still flogged—outwardly light, inwardly killing.

sentences.zh: 祖宗鑒既往之弊，蠲除煩苛，始用折杖之法，新天下耳目，茲蓋曠古聖賢，思所未至，陛下深惻民隱，親覽庶獄。

translations.literal: The founding emperors took warning from past harm, abolished troublesome severity, and began the commuted-staff method—new to the realm's eyes; this is what ancient sages never thought of; Your Majesty deeply pities the people's hardship and personally views common cases.
translations.idiomatic: The founders took warning from past harm, abolished severity, and began commuted-staff punishment—new to the realm; Your Majesty deeply pities the people and personally views cases.

sentences.zh: 歷世用刑，無如本朝之平恕，宜乎天降之祥。

translations.literal: Penal use through the ages has none so mild and forgiving as our dynasty—Heaven's auspiciousness should descend.
translations.idiomatic: Penal use through the ages has none so mild as our dynasty—Heaven's auspiciousness should descend.

sentences.zh: 而方當隆盛之時，未享繼嗣之慶，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Yet at the time of flourishing grandeur we have not enjoyed the joy of succession—I am privately puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at flourishing grandeur we have not enjoyed succession—I am puzzled.

sentences.zh: 或者宦官太多，而陛下未悟也。

translations.literal: Perhaps eunuchs are too many and Your Majesty has not awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps eunuchs are too many and Your Majesty has not awakened.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 肉刑之五，一曰宮，古人除之，重絕人之世。

translations.literal: Of the five flesh punishments one is castration; the ancients abolished it, weightily ending a man's line.
translations.idiomatic: Of the five flesh punishments castration was abolished by the ancients, weightily ending a man's line.

sentences.zh: 今則宦官之家，競求他子，剿絕人理，希求爵命。

translations.literal: Now eunuch families compete to seek other men's sons, cutting off human principle and hoping for rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now eunuch families compete for other men's sons, cutting off human principle for rank.

sentences.zh: 童幼何罪，隱於刀鋸，因而夭死者，未易悉數。

translations.literal: What crime have infants that they hide in knife and saw and thus die young—the number is not easy to count fully.
translations.idiomatic: What crime have infants hidden in knife and saw who die young—countless.

sentences.zh: 夫有疾而夭，治世所羞，況無疾乎？

translations.literal: To die young from illness is a shame in a well-governed age—how much more without illness?
translations.idiomatic: To die young from illness shames a well-governed age—how much more without illness?

sentences.zh: 有罪而宮，前王不忍，況無罪乎？

translations.literal: To castrate the guilty former kings could not bear—how much more the guiltless?
translations.idiomatic: To castrate the guilty former kings could not bear—how much more the guiltless?

sentences.zh: 臣聞漢永平之際，中常侍四員，小黃門十人爾。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in Han's Yongping there were four Regular Palace Attendants and ten Yellow Gate attendants only.
translations.idiomatic: In Han's Yongping there were four Regular Palace Attendants and ten Yellow Gate attendants only.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗定制，無得逾百員。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang fixed the system—none might exceed a hundred posts.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Taizong fixed the system—none might exceed a hundred posts.

sentences.zh: 且以祖宗近事較之，祖宗時宦官凡幾何人，今凡幾何人？

translations.literal: Comparing with a near matter of the founding emperors—how many eunuchs then, how many now?
translations.idiomatic: Comparing founding times—how many eunuchs then, how many now?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以謂胎卵傷而鳳凰不至，宦官多而繼嗣未育也。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that when eggs are harmed the phoenix does not come; when eunuchs are many succession is not bred.
translations.idiomatic: When eggs are harmed the phoenix does not come; when eunuchs are many succession is not bred.

sentences.zh: 伏望順陽春生育之令，浚發德音，詳為條禁。

translations.literal: I bow and hope to follow spring's nurturing order, issue virtuous sound, and detail prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: I hope to follow spring's nurturing order, issue virtuous sound, and detail prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 進獻宦官，一切權罷，擅宮童幼，置以重法。

translations.literal: Presented eunuchs—all temporarily stop; those who privately castrate youths—establish heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: Presented eunuchs—all temporarily stop; private castration of youths—heavy law.

sentences.zh: 若然，則天心必應，聖嗣必廣，召福祥、安宗廟之策，無先於此。」

translations.literal: If so Heaven's heart will respond, holy succession will broaden, and the policy to summon fortune and settle the altars has nothing before this."
translations.idiomatic: If so Heaven will respond, succession will broaden, and no policy summons fortune and settles the altars before this."

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝異其言，欲用為諫官，而及以父憂去。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor marveled at his words and wished to make him remonstrance officer, but Ji left on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and wished to make him remonstrance officer, but Ji left on father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，始擢秘閣校理，逾月，改右正言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou he was first promoted Secretariat collator; after a month he was changed to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou's third year he was promoted Secretariat collator; after a month Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 復上疏曰：「帝王之治，必敦骨肉之愛，而以至親夾輔王室。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Imperial governance must thicken flesh-and-blood love and use the closest kin to support the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized, "Governance must thicken kinship love and use closest kin to support the royal house.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『懷德惟寧，宗子惟城。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Cherish virtue then peace; clansmen are the wall.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Cherish virtue then peace; clansmen are the wall.'

sentences.zh: 故同姓者，國家之屏翰；

translations.literal: Thus same-surname kin are the state's screen;
translations.idiomatic: Thus same-surname kin are the state's screen;

sentences.zh: 儲副者，天下之根本。

translations.literal: the heir is the realm's root.
translations.idiomatic: the heir is the realm's root.

sentences.zh: 陛下以海宇之廣，宗廟之重，而根本未立，四方無所係心，上下之憂，無大於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with the sea's breadth and the altars' weight yet the root is not established—the realm has nowhere to fix its heart; no worry is greater above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty with the sea's breadth and altars' weight yet no root established—the realm has nowhere to fix its heart; no worry is greater.

sentences.zh: 謂宜發自聖斷，擇宗室子以備儲副。

translations.literal: I say an edict should issue from the sacred resolve to choose a clansman to prepare as heir.
translations.idiomatic: An edict should issue from sacred resolve to choose a clansman as heir.

sentences.zh: 以服屬議之，則莫如親；

translations.literal: Discussing by kinship, none is closer than kin;
translations.idiomatic: By kinship none is closer than kin;

sentences.zh: 以人望言之，則莫如賢。

translations.literal: discussing by public expectation, none is like the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: by public expectation none like the worthy.

sentences.zh: 既兼親賢，然後優封爵以寵異之，選重厚樸茂之臣以教導之，聽入侍禁中，示欲為後，使中外之人悚然瞻望，曰：『宮中有子矣。』

translations.literal: Having both kinship and worth, then generously enfeoff with noble rank to favor them, choose heavy, honest, plain, and substantial ministers to instruct, allow attendance in the forbidden palace, show intent to make heir, so inside and outside look in awe and say: 'Within the palace there is a son.'
translations.idiomatic: Having both kin and worth, enfeoff generously, choose heavy honest ministers to instruct, allow palace attendance, show intent to make heir, so all say, 'Within the palace there is a son.'

sentences.zh: 陛下他日有嫡嗣，則異其恩禮，復令歸邸，於理無嫌，於義為順，弭覬覦之心，屬天下之望，宗廟長久之策也。」

translations.literal: If later Your Majesty has a legitimate heir, then differ in favor and ritual and order return to residence—in principle no taint, in righteousness compliant, quelling covetous hearts, binding the realm's hope—long policy for the altars.
translations.idiomatic: If later a legitimate heir comes, differ in favor and order return to residence—no taint in principle, compliant in righteousness, quelling covetous hearts, binding the realm's hope—long policy for the altars.

sentences.zh: 既而又言：「開寶詔書：『內侍臣年三十無養父者，聽養一子為嗣，並以名上宣徽院，違者抵死。』

translations.literal: He again said: "The Kaibao edict: 'Inner attendants at thirty without an adoptive father may adopt one son as heir and report the name to the Palace Treasury Bureau—violators die.
translations.idiomatic: He again cited the Kaibao edict: 'Inner attendants at thirty without adoptive father may adopt one son and report to the Palace Treasury—violators die.

sentences.zh: 比年此禁益弛，夭絕人理，陰累聖嗣。

translations.literal: In recent years this prohibition has grown lax, cutting off human principle and secretly burdening holy succession.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this prohibition grew lax, cutting human principle and burdening succession.

sentences.zh: 願詔大臣明示舊制，上順天意，以綏福祐。」

translations.literal: I wish an edict to great ministers clearly showing the old system, following Heaven's intent to extend fortune and blessing."
translations.idiomatic: I wish an edict to great ministers showing the old system, following Heaven to extend blessing."

sentences.zh: 明年，遂權罷內臣進養子。

translations.literal: The next year inner attendants presenting adoptive sons was temporarily stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year presenting adoptive sons to inner attendants was stopped.

sentences.zh: 管勾登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He managed the Dengwen Inspection Court.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the Dengwen Inspection Court.

sentences.zh: 又上書論政事，謂：「倉廩空虛，內外匱乏，其弊在於官多兵冗。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on government affairs, saying: "Granaries are empty, inside and outside exhausted—the harm lies in many officials and redundant troops.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized, "Granaries are empty, inside and outside exhausted—the harm is many officials and redundant troops.

sentences.zh: 請汰冗兵，省冗官，然後除民之疾苦。」

translations.literal: I ask to prune redundant troops and cut redundant officials, then remove the people's hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Prune redundant troops and cut redundant officials, then remove the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 因條上十餘事，多施用之。

translations.literal: He then listed more than ten items—many were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He listed more than ten items—many were implemented.

sentences.zh: 建請擇館職，分校館閣書，並求遺書於天下，語在《藝文志》。

translations.literal: He proposed selecting pavilion scholars to divide school-pavilion books and seek lost books throughout the realm—the account is in the Treatise on Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed selecting pavilion scholars to divide library books and seek lost books throughout the realm—as in the Treatise on Literature.

sentences.zh: 明年，日食三朝，及言：「日食者，陰侵陽之戒。

translations.literal: The next year there was a solar eclipse at the third audience; Ji again said: "Solar eclipse is yin's encroachment on yang's warning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a solar eclipse came at the third audience; Ji said, "Solar eclipse warns yin encroaching on yang.

sentences.zh: 在人事，則臣陵君，妻乘夫，四夷侵中國。

translations.literal: In human affairs ministers override the ruler, wives override husbands, the four barbarians invade China.
translations.idiomatic: In human affairs ministers override rulers, wives override husbands, barbarians invade China.

sentences.zh: 今大臣無姑息之政，非所謂臣陵君，失在陛下淵默臨朝，使陰邪未盡屏也。

translations.literal: Now great ministers have no indulgent government—this is not ministers overriding the ruler; the failure is Your Majesty's deep silence in audience so hidden evil is not fully expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers have no indulgent government—not ministers overriding the ruler; the failure is deep silence so hidden evil is not expelled.

sentences.zh: 后妃無權橫之家，非所謂妻乘夫，失在左右親倖，驕縱亡節也。

translations.literal: The empress has no powerful family—this is not wives overriding husbands; the failure is close favorites on left and right arrogantly breaking discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The empress has no powerful family—not wives overriding husbands; the failure is close favorites arrogantly breaking discipline.

sentences.zh: 疆埸無虞，非所謂四夷侵中國，失在將帥非其人，為敵所輕也。」

translations.literal: The borders are without alarm—this is not barbarians invading China; the failure is generals not the right men and enemies hold us light."
translations.idiomatic: Borders lack alarm—not barbarians invading; the failure is wrong generals and enemies hold us light."

sentences.zh: 因言孫沔在幷州，苛暴不法，燕飲無度；

translations.literal: He then said Sun Hao in Bing Prefecture was harsh and unlawful and feasted without limit;
translations.idiomatic: He said Sun Hao in Bing Prefecture was harsh, unlawful, and feasted without limit;

sentences.zh: 龐藉前在幷州，輕動寡謀，輒興堡砦，屈野之衄，為國深恥。

translations.literal: Pang Ji earlier in Bing Prefecture acted lightly with little counsel and rashly raised forts—the defeat at Quye was deep shame to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji earlier in Bing acted lightly, rashly raised forts—the Quye defeat was deep national shame.

sentences.zh: 沔繇此坐廢。

translations.literal: Hao was thereby dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「春秋有告糴，陛下恩施動植，視人如傷。

translations.literal: He again said: "In spring and autumn there is reporting of grain need; Your Majesty's grace moves living things and views people as wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He again said, "Spring and autumn report grain need; Your Majesty's grace views people as wounded.

sentences.zh: 然州郡官司各專其民，擅造閉糴之令，一路饑，則鄰路為之閉糴；

translations.literal: Yet prefectural officials each hold their people and arbitrarily make closed-grain orders—one circuit famines and the neighboring circuit closes grain;
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefectural officials hold their people and make closed-grain orders—one circuit famines and neighbors close grain;

sentences.zh: 一郡饑，則鄰郡為之閉糴。

translations.literal: one prefecture famines and the neighboring prefecture closes grain.
translations.idiomatic: one prefecture famines and neighbors close grain.

sentences.zh: 夫二千石以上，所宜同國休戚，而坐視流離，豈聖朝子育兆民之意哉！」

translations.literal: Those above two thousand bushels should share the state's joy and sorrow yet sit watching displacement—is this the holy court's nurturing of the multitude?"
translations.idiomatic: Officials above two thousand bushels should share state joy and sorrow yet watch displacement—is this nurturing the multitude?"

sentences.zh: 遂詔：「鄰州、鄰路災傷而輒閉糴，論如違制律。」

translations.literal: An edict then said: "Neighboring prefectures and circuits that close grain when disaster strikes shall be judged under the law of violating controls."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled neighboring prefectures and circuits closing grain in disaster shall be judged under violating controls.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷右司諫、管勾國子監。

translations.literal: After long service he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Officer and managed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was Right Remonstrance Officer and managed the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，以勁正稱，遇事無小大輒言。

translations.literal: In office several years he was known for firm uprightness and spoke on affairs great and small.
translations.idiomatic: Several years in office he was known for firm uprightness and spoke on all affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗請毋納群臣上尊號，出後宮私身及非執事人，毋以御寶白劄子賜近幸家人冠帔及比丘尼紫衣；

translations.literal: He once asked not to receive ministers' honorific titles, to send out private palace women and non-official persons, not to use the imperial seal on white memo to bestow on close favorites' families caps and sashes and on Buddhist nuns purple robes;
translations.idiomatic: He asked not to receive honorific titles, to send out private palace women and non-officials, not to use imperial seal on white memo for favorites' families or nuns' purple robes;

sentences.zh: 並責執政大臣因循苟簡，畏避怨謗，宜用唐李吉甫故事，選拔賢俊，約杜預遺法，旌擢守令；

translations.literal: and charged assisting great ministers for following along, crude and simple, fearing and avoiding resentment—should use Tang Li Jifu's precedent to select worthy men and roughly Du Yu's leftover method to elevate prefects and magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: and charged ministers for following along, fearing resentment—use Tang Li Jifu's precedent to select worthies and Du Yu's method to elevate prefects;

sentences.zh: 復置將作監官屬，專領營造；

translations.literal: restore Directorate of Palace Buildings posts to specialize in construction;
translations.idiomatic: restore Palace Buildings posts for construction;

sentences.zh: 論入內都知任守忠陵轢駙馬都尉李瑋及干求內降。

translations.literal: discussed Inner Palace Director Ren Shouzhong's bullying of the imperial son-in-law Li Wei and seeking inner edicts.
translations.idiomatic: discussed Inner Palace Director Ren Shouzhong bullying imperial son-in-law Li Wei and seeking inner edicts.

sentences.zh: 會諫官陳升之建請裁節班行補授，下兩制、臺諫官集議。

translations.literal: When Remonstrance Officer Chen Shengzhi proposed trimming roster supplemental appointments, it was sent to the two Hanlin academies and remonstrance and censor officials for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shengzhi proposed trimming roster supplements, the two Hanlin academies and remonstrance and censors deliberated jointly.

sentences.zh: 主鐵冶者，舊得補班行。

translations.literal: Those managing iron smelting formerly could supplement roster entry.
translations.idiomatic: Iron smelting managers formerly could supplement roster entry.

sentences.zh: 至是，議罷之。

translations.literal: At this point it was deliberated to abolish.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 既定稿，及與御史沈起輒增注興國軍磁湖鐵冶如舊制。

translations.literal: When the draft was fixed Ji and Censor Shen Qi added a note restoring Cixing Army's Cihu iron smelting as in the old system.
translations.idiomatic: When the draft was fixed Ji and Censor Shen Qi added a note restoring Cihu iron smelting as before.

sentences.zh: 主磁湖冶者，大姓程叔良也。

translations.literal: The manager of Cihu smelting was the great clan Cheng Shuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Cihu's manager was the great clan Cheng Shuliang.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士胡宿等即劾及與起職在臺諫，而為程氏經營占錮恩例，請詔問狀，皆引伏。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Hu Su and others at once impeached Ji and Qi for holding remonstrance and censor posts yet working for the Cheng clan to monopolize favor—requested edict inquiry; all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Hu Su impeached Ji and Qi for holding censor posts yet working for the Cheng clan—edict inquiry; all confessed.

sentences.zh: 及出為工部員外郎、知廬州，進戶部、直昭文館、知桂州。

translations.literal: Ji was sent out as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works governing Luzhou, promoted to Household Ministry and Attendant of the Bright Literary Hall governing Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was sent out as Outer Gentleman of Works governing Luzhou, promoted to Household Ministry and Bright Literary Attendant governing Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，錄其弟齊為太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: He died; his younger brother Qi was enrolled as Grand Temple Acolyte.
translations.idiomatic: He died; younger brother Qi was enrolled as Grand Temple Acolyte.

sentences.zh: 及當官有守，初為檢法官，三司請重鑄鐵錢法至死。

translations.literal: Ji in office had integrity; when first examining judge the Three Offices asked to re-cast iron coin law with death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had integrity in office; as examining judge the Three Offices asked death penalty for re-casting iron coin law.

sentences.zh: 下有司議，及爭不可，主者恚曰：「立天下法，當由一檢法邪？」

translations.literal: It went to offices for deliberation; Ji argued it could not be—the chief was angry: "Establishing law under Heaven—should one examining judge decide?"
translations.idiomatic: Offices deliberated; Ji argued no—the chief was angry: "Establishing law under Heaven—should one examining judge decide?"

sentences.zh: 及曰：「義理為先，安有高下？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Right principle comes first—how can there be high and low?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Right principle comes first—how can there be high and low?"

sentences.zh: 卒不為詘。

translations.literal: In the end he was not bent.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was not bent.

sentences.zh: 范師道

translations.literal: Fan Shidao
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shidao

sentences.zh: 范師道，字貫之，蘇州長洲人。

translations.literal: Fan Shidao, courtesy name Guanzhi, was a native of Changzhou in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shidao, whose courtesy name was Guanzhi, came from Changzhou in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為撫州判官，後知廣德縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and was adjutant of Fuzhou, later governing Guangde County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, was adjutant of Fuzhou, later governed Guangde County.

sentences.zh: 縣有張王廟，民歲祠神，殺牛數千，師道禁絕之。

translations.literal: The county had the Zhang King temple; the people yearly sacrificed to the god and killed several thousand cattle; Shidao forbade it completely.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the Zhang King temple where people yearly sacrificed and killed thousands of cattle; Shidao forbade it.

sentences.zh: 通判許州，累遷都官員外郎，吳育舉為御史。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Xu Prefecture he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Wu Yu recommended him as censor.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Xu he rose to Outer Gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Wu Yu recommended him as censor.

sentences.zh: 奏請罷內降推恩，擇宰相久其任，選宗室賢者養宮中備儲貳。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to stop inner edicts of grace, choose chief councillors of long tenure, and select worthy clansmen to rear in the palace as heir reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to stop inner grace edicts, choose long-serving chief councillors, and rear worthy clansmen in the palace as heir reserve.

sentences.zh: 初，皇祐中，賈昌朝上議置五輔郡，設京畿轉運使、提點刑獄，號為「拱輔京師」，而論者謂宦官謀廣親事親從兵，欲取京畿財賦贍之，因以收事柄。

translations.literal: Initially in Huangyou Jia Changchao above deliberated establishing five auxiliary prefectures, setting metropolitan transport and judicial intendant posts, called "bowing to support the capital"—discussants said eunuchs plotted to broaden kin soldiers' support and take metropolitan wealth to nourish them, thereby seizing power.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou Jia Changchao proposed five auxiliary prefectures with metropolitan transport and judicial posts, called "bowing to support the capital"—discussants said eunuchs sought kin soldiers and metropolitan wealth to seize power.

sentences.zh: 師道力奏非便，遂復舊制。

translations.literal: Shidao memorialized forcefully that it was not convenient and the old system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao forcefully memorialized against it and the old system was restored.

sentences.zh: 又以四年貢舉，士苦淹久，請易為三年。

translations.literal: He also because the four-year examination made scholars suffer long delay asked to change to three years.
translations.idiomatic: Because the four-year examination made scholars wait too long he asked three years.

sentences.zh: 宰相劉沆護葬溫成皇后，禮官議稱「陵」，師道以為非典制，數以爭，沆惡之，引著令「臺官滿二年當補外」，出知常州。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Liu Kang oversaw burial of Empress Wen Cheng; ritual officers deliberated calling it "tomb"; Shidao thought it not canonical and argued several times; Kang hated him and cited the rule "censors after two full years should supplement outside"—sent out to govern Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kang oversaw Empress Wen Cheng's burial; ritual officers called it "tomb"; Shidao argued it was uncanonical; Kang cited the rule censors after two years go outside—sent him to Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臺諫官共言師道不當去，不報。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and censor officials jointly said Shidao should not leave—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and censors said Shidao should not leave—no reply.

sentences.zh: 徙廣南東路轉運使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangnan East Circuit transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangnan East Circuit transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舊補攝官皆委吏胥，無先後遠近之差，師道為置籍次第之。

translations.literal: Formerly supplemental officials were all entrusted to clerks without order of priority near or far; Shidao made registers to sequence them.
translations.idiomatic: Supplemental officials had been entrusted to clerks without order; Shidao sequenced them in registers.

sentences.zh: 召為鹽鐵判官，道改兩浙轉運使，遷起居舍人、同知諫院，管勾國子監。

translations.literal: Summoned as Salt and Iron adjudicator, on the road changed to Liangzhe transport commissioner, promoted to Drafting Attendant and joint manager of the Remonstrance Bureau, managing the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Salt and Iron adjudicator, en route changed to Liangzhe transport commissioner, promoted to Drafting Attendant joint-managing Remonstrance Bureau and Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 後宮周氏、董氏生公主，諸閣女御多遷擢。

translations.literal: Later the inner palace's Lady Zhou and Lady Dong bore princesses and many inner attendants were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ladies Zhou and Dong bore princesses and many inner attendants were promoted.

sentences.zh: 師道上疏曰：

translations.literal: Shidao memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Shidao memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「禮以制情，義以奪愛，常人之所難，惟聰明睿哲之主然後能之。

translations.literal: "Ritual regulates emotion, righteousness overcomes love—what is hard for ordinary people only enlightened and sagely rulers can do.
translations.idiomatic: "Ritual regulates emotion, righteousness overcomes love—ordinary people find it hard; only enlightened rulers can.

sentences.zh: 近以宮人數多而出之，此盛德事也。

translations.literal: Recently because palace women were numerous some were sent out—this is a great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Recently many palace women were sent out—great virtue.

sentences.zh: 然而事有係風化治亂之大，而未以留意，臣敢為陛下言之。

translations.literal: Yet affairs touching great customs and the order of governance and chaos have not received attention—I dare speak for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs touching customs and order of governance have not received attention—I dare speak.

sentences.zh: 竊聞諸閣女御，以周、董育公主，御寶白劄並為才人，不自中書出誥。

translations.literal: I hear that because Ladies Zhou and Dong bore princesses, imperial white memos all made them Talents without edicts from the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ladies Zhou and Dong bore princesses, white memos made inner attendants Talents without Secretariat edicts.

sentences.zh: 而掖庭覬覦遷拜者甚多，周、董之遷可矣，女御何名而遷乎？

translations.literal: In the inner quarters many hope for promotion by observation—Zhou and Dong's promotion may be, but what name do inner attendants have to be promoted?
translations.idiomatic: Many in the inner quarters hope for promotion—Zhou and Dong may be promoted, but what name for inner attendants?

sentences.zh: 才人品秩既高，古有定員，唐制止七人而已。

translations.literal: Talent rank is already high; antiquity had fixed quotas—Tang stopped at seven only.
translations.idiomatic: Talent rank is already high; antiquity fixed quotas—Tang stopped at seven.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝宮闈給侍不過二三百，居五品之列者無幾，若使諸閣皆遷，則不復更有員數矣。

translations.literal: In the founding reign inner service was not more than two or three hundred; those at fifth rank were few—if all inner halls are promoted there will be no quota left.
translations.idiomatic: Founding inner service was under two or three hundred; fifth rank was few—if all inner halls promote, no quota remains.

sentences.zh: 外人不能詳知，止謂陛下於寵幸太過，恩澤不節耳。

translations.literal: Outsiders cannot know in detail and only say Your Majesty favors too much and grace is unbounded.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders only say Your Majesty favors too much and grace is unbounded.

sentences.zh: 夫婦人女子，與小人之性同，寵幸太過，則瀆慢之心生，恩澤不節，則無厭之怨起，御之不可不以其道也。

translations.literal: Women and petty men's natures are the same—favor too much and irreverent hearts arise; grace unbounded and discontented resentment rises—one cannot rule them without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Women and petty men share nature—too much favor breeds irreverence; unbounded grace breeds resentment—they must be ruled by the Way.

sentences.zh: 且用度太煩，須索太廣，一才人之奉，月直中戶百家之賦，歲時賜予不在焉。

translations.literal: Moreover expenditures are too troublesome and demands too broad—one Talent's monthly support equals a hundred middle households' tax; yearly gifts are besides.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditures are troublesome—one Talent's monthly support equals a hundred households' tax, yearly gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 況誥命之出，不自有司，豈盛時之事耶？

translations.literal: Moreover edict appointment does not come from the offices—is this a flourishing age's affair?
translations.idiomatic: Edict appointment does not come from offices—is this a flourishing age?

sentences.zh: 恐斜封、墨敕，復見於今日矣。」

translations.literal: I fear irregular sealed appointments and ink edicts will again appear today."
translations.idiomatic: I fear irregular sealed appointments and ink edicts will reappear today."

sentences.zh: 時大星隕東南，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: At the time a great star fell in the southeast with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: A great star fell southeast with thunderous sound.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「《漢》、《晉天文志》：『天狗所下，為破軍殺將，伏屍流血。』

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "The Han and Jin astronomical treatises: 'Where the celestial dog falls, generals are broken, armies killed, corpses lie and blood flows.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized, "Han and Jin astronomical treatises: 'Where the celestial dog falls, generals break, armies die, blood flows.

sentences.zh: 《甘氏圖》：『天狗移，大賊起。』

translations.literal: The Gan clan chart: 'When the celestial dog moves, great bandits rise.'
translations.idiomatic: The Gan chart: 'When the celestial dog moves, great bandits rise.'

sentences.zh: 今朝廷非無為之時也，而備邊防盜，未見其至。

translations.literal: Now the court is not without action yet border defense against bandits is not seen arriving.
translations.idiomatic: The court is not inactive yet border defense is not seen.

sentences.zh: 雖有將帥，不老則愚，士卒雖多，勁勇者少。

translations.literal: Though there are generals, if old then foolish; though soldiers are many, the bold and brave are few.
translations.idiomatic: There are generals, but if old then foolish; soldiers are many, but the bold are few.

sentences.zh: 小人思亂，伺隙乃作，必有包藏險心，投隙而動者。

translations.literal: Petty men think of disorder and watch for gaps to act—surely some harbor hidden dangerous hearts and will move when a gap appears.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men think of disorder and watch for gaps—some harbor dangerous hearts and will act.

sentences.zh: 宜揀拔將帥，訓練卒伍，詔天下預為備禦。」

translations.literal: Generals should be selected and troops trained; edict the realm to prepare in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Select generals, train troops, edict the realm to prepare."

sentences.zh: 仁宗晚年尤恭儉，而四方無事，師道言雖過，每優容之。

translations.literal: In Renzong's late years he was especially respectful and frugal and the realm was without affairs—Shidao's words though excessive were each treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's late years he was especially frugal and the realm was peaceful—Shidao's words, though excessive, were indulged.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事、判都水監。

translations.literal: Transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of War concurrently Attending Censor with supervisory duties adjudicating Metropolitan Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Outer Gentleman of War with supervisory censor duties over Metropolitan Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 與諫官、御史數奏樞密副使陳升之不當用，升之罷，師道亦出知福州。

translations.literal: With remonstrance officers and censors he several times memorialized that Vice Bureau Commissioner Chen Shengzhi should not be used; Shengzhi was dismissed and Shidao was also sent out to govern Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With remonstrators and censors he several times said Vice Commissioner Chen Shengzhi should not be used; Shengzhi was dismissed and Shidao sent to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以工部郎中入為三司鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: Before long as Department Gentleman he entered as Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Soon as Department Gentleman he became Vice Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 感風眩，遷戶部，直龍圖閣、知明州，卒。

translations.literal: Struck by wind dizziness he was transferred to the Household Ministry, Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall governing Ming Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by vertigo he transferred to Household Ministry, Dragon Diagram Attendant governing Ming Prefecture, and died.

sentences.zh: 師道厲風操，前後在言責，有聞即言，或獨爭，或列奏。

translations.literal: Shidao was stern in wind and integrity; before and in remonstrance office when he heard something he spoke, sometimes arguing alone or listing memorials together.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was stern and upright; in remonstrance office he spoke when he heard, sometimes alone, sometimes jointly.

sentences.zh: 如陳執中家人殺婢，卒坐免；

translations.literal: Such as when Chen Zhizhong's household killed a maid he was finally dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhizhong's household killed a maid he was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 奪王拱辰宣徽使、李淑翰林學士；

translations.literal: stripped Wang Gongchen of Palatial Affairs Commissioner and Li Shu of Hanlin Academician;
translations.idiomatic: stripped Wang Gongchen of Palatial Affairs and Li Shu of Hanlin;

sentences.zh: 及王德用、程戡領樞密，宦官石全彬、閻士良升進，皆嘗奏數其罪焉。

translations.literal: and when Wang Deyong and Cheng Kan held the Bureau and eunuchs Shi Quanbin and Yan Shiliang were promoted—all were several times memorialized for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: when Wang Deyong and Cheng Kan held the Bureau and eunuchs Shi Quanbin and Yan Shiliang rose—all were memorialized for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 李絢，字公素，邛州依政人。

translations.literal: Li Xuan, courtesy name Gongsu, was a native of Yizheng in Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan, whose courtesy name was Gongsu, came from Yizheng in Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少放蕩亡檢，兄綯教之書，嚴其課業而出，絢遨自若，比暮綯歸，絢徐取書視之，一過輒誦數千言，綯奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he was unrestrained without restraint; his elder brother Chao taught him books, strictly supervised his lessons and sent him out; Xuan roamed at ease and when evening Chao returned Xuan slowly took books and after one reading could recite several thousand words—Chao marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Youthfully unrestrained, elder brother Chao taught and strictly supervised him; Xuan roamed freely and when Chao returned evenings Xuan read once and recited thousands of words—Chao marveled.

sentences.zh: 稍長，能屬文，尤工歌詩。

translations.literal: When slightly grown he could compose prose and was especially skilled at songs and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he composed prose and excelled at poetry.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事被繫，既而逸去。

translations.literal: Once because of an affair he was imprisoned and then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once imprisoned for an affair, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，再授大理評事、通判邠州。

translations.literal: Placed in the jinshi he was twice made an evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Placed in the jinshi he twice served as Court of Judicial Review evaluator and vice-prefect of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊犯延州，幷邊皆恐。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao invaded Yan Prefecture the entire border was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao invaded Yan Prefecture the border was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 邠城陴不完，絢方攝守，即發民治城，僚吏皆謂當言上逮報，絢不聽。

translations.literal: Bin's walls were incomplete; Xuan was acting defender and at once mobilized the people to repair the city; subordinate officials all said they should report upward and await reply—Xuan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's walls were incomplete; Xuan acting defender mobilized repairs; subordinates said report upward—Xuan refused.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之喜，因詔他州悉治守備。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was pleased and therefore edicted other prefectures all to repair defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and edicted other prefectures to repair defenses.

sentences.zh: 還為太子中允、直集賢院，歷開封府推官、三司度支判官，為京西轉運使。

translations.literal: On return he was Heir Apparent Vice Director and Attendant of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, successively Kaifeng adjudicator and Three Offices fiscal adjudicator, and Jingxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was Heir Apparent Vice Director and Hall Attendant, then Kaifeng adjudicator, Three Offices fiscal adjudicator, and Jingxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，范雍知河南，王舉正知許州，任中師知陳州，任布知河陽，並二府舊臣，絢皆以不才奏之。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Yong governed Henan, Wang Juzheng governed Xu Prefecture, Ren Zhongshi governed Chen Prefecture, Ren Bu governed Heyang—all were old ministers of the two departments; Xuan memorialized them all as without talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yong governed Henan, Wang Juzheng Xu, Ren Zhongshi Chen, Ren Bu Heyang—all two-department veterans; Xuan memorialized them all as without talent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召修起居注，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to compile the Draft Diary and investigate capital punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he compiled the Draft Diary and investigated capital punishments.

sentences.zh: 時宰相杜衍各拔知名士置臺省，惡衍者指絢為其黨。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Councillor Du Yan each pulled famous scholars into the Censorate and Secretariat; those who hated Yan pointed at Xuan as his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Du Yan placed famous scholars in Censorate and Secretariat; Yan's enemies called Xuan his faction.

sentences.zh: 絢嘗舉陸經，經坐贓貶；

translations.literal: Xuan once recommended Lu Jing; Jing was demoted for corruption;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan once recommended Lu Jing, who was demoted for corruption;

sentences.zh: 而任布又言絢在京西苛察，出知潤州。

translations.literal: and Ren Bu also said Xuan was harsh in investigation in Jingxi—sent out to govern Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Bu also said Xuan was harsh in Jingxi—sent to Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改太常丞，徙洪州。

translations.literal: Changed to Grand Temple Director, transferred to Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Changed to Grand Temple Director, transferred to Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時五溪蠻寇湖南，擇轉運使，帝曰：「有館職善飲酒者為誰，今安在？」

translations.literal: At the time the Five Streams barbarians raided Hunan; choosing a transport commissioner the emperor said: "Which pavilion officer is good at drinking, where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: Five Streams barbarians raided Hunan; choosing transport commissioner the emperor said, "Which pavilion officer drinks well—where is he?"

sentences.zh: 輔臣未諭，帝曰：「是往歲城邠州者，其人才可用。」

translations.literal: Assisting ministers did not understand; the emperor said: "It is he who walled Bin Prefecture years ago—his talent can be used."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers did not understand; the emperor said, "He who walled Bin years ago—his talent can be used."

sentences.zh: 輔臣以絢對，遂除湖南轉運使。

translations.literal: Assisting ministers answered with Xuan and he was made Hunan transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers named Xuan and he became Hunan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 絢乘驛至邵州，戒諸部按兵毋得動，使人諭蠻以禍福，蠻罷兵受約束。

translations.literal: Xuan rode post-horses to Shaozhou, warned all departments to hold troops and not move, sent men to tell the barbarians fortune and misfortune—the barbarians ceased arms and accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rode to Shaozhou, warned departments to hold troops, told barbarians fortune and misfortune—they ceased arms and accepted restraint.

sentences.zh: 復修起居注，權判三司鹽鐵勾院，復糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: Again he compiled the Draft Diary, acted over Salt and Iron Audit Office, and again investigated capital punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Again he compiled the Draft Diary, acted over Salt and Iron Audit, and again investigated capital punishments.

sentences.zh: 以右正言、知制誥奉使契丹，知審官院，遷龍圖閣直學士、起居舍人、權知開封府，治有能名。

translations.literal: As Right Rectifier and Drafting Gentleman he was envoy to the Khitan, managed the Court of Official Appointment, was promoted to Dragon Diagram Attendant, Drafting Attendant, acting Kaifeng—his governance had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Rectifier and Drafting Gentleman he was Khitan envoy, managed Court of Official Appointment, rose to Dragon Diagram Attendant, Drafting Attendant, acting Kaifeng—governance had ability.

sentences.zh: 絢夜醉，晨奏事酒未解，帝曰：「開封府事劇，豈可沉湎於酒邪？」

translations.literal: Xuan was drunk at night; in the morning memorializing affairs the wine had not cleared; the emperor said: "Kaifeng affairs are pressing—how can one sink in wine?"
translations.idiomatic: Drunk at night, memorializing in the morning still drunk, the emperor said, "Kaifeng affairs are pressing—how sink in wine?"

sentences.zh: 改提舉在京諸司庫務，權判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: Changed to commissioner of metropolitan storehouses, acting over the Board of Personnel Outside Register.
translations.idiomatic: Changed to metropolitan storehouse commissioner, acting over Board of Personnel Outside Register.

sentences.zh: 初，慈孝寺亡章獻太后神御物，盜得，而絢誤釋之，詘知蘇州，未行，卒。

translations.literal: Initially at Cixiao Temple the sacred objects of Empress Zhangxian were stolen and recovered; Xuan mistakenly released them and was demoted to govern Suzhou; before setting out he died.
translations.idiomatic: At Cixiao Temple Empress Zhangxian's sacred objects were stolen and recovered; Xuan mistakenly released them, was demoted to Suzhou, and died before setting out.

sentences.zh: 絢疏明樂易，少周遊四方，頗練世務。

translations.literal: Xuan was open and easygoing; in youth he traveled widely and was quite practiced in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was open and easygoing, traveled widely in youth, and knew worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 數上書言便宜。

translations.literal: He several times memorialized on convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He several times memorialized practical proposals.

sentences.zh: 仁宗春秋高，未有繼嗣，絢因祀高禖還獻賦，大指言宜遠嬖寵，近賢良，則神降之福，子孫繁衍，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Renzong's years were high and there was no heir, Xuan on returning from sacrificing to Gaoxi presented a fu—its main point said to distance favorites and draw near worthy men, then divine blessing and sons and grandsons would multiply—the emperor praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong had no heir, Xuan returning from Gaoxi sacrifice presented a fu urging distance from favorites and nearness to worthies—then blessing and succession would multiply—the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，終以疾死。

translations.literal: His nature loved wine and he finally died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and finally died of illness.

sentences.zh: 何中立

translations.literal: He Zhongli
translations.idiomatic: He Zhongli

sentences.zh: 何中立，字公南，許州長社人。

translations.literal: He Zhongli, courtesy name Gongnan, was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhongli, whose courtesy name was Gongnan, came from Changshe in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼警邁，與狄遵度遊，遵度曰：「美才也！」

translations.literal: In youth he was sharp and advanced; traveling with Di Zundu, Zundu said: "A fine talent!"
translations.idiomatic: Sharp in youth, traveling with Di Zundu, Zundu said, "Fine talent!"

sentences.zh: 其父棐遂以女妻之。

translations.literal: His father Fei then gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fei then gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，授大理評事，歷僉書鎮安、武勝二鎮節度判官，遷殿中丞，召試學士院，為集賢校理。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi, was made an evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, successively signed as adjutant of Zhen'an and Wusheng military commissions, was transferred to Defender-in-Chief of the Palace Administration, was summoned to test at the Hanlin Academy, and became Collator of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, was Court of Judicial Review evaluator, signed Zhen'an and Wusheng adjutancies, became Defender-in-Chief, tested at Hanlin, and became Hall collator.

sentences.zh: 改太常博士、修起居注，遷祠部員外郎、知制誥，權發遣開封府事。

translations.literal: Changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler of the Draft Diary, transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Drafting Gentleman, with dispatched authority over Kaifeng affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Changed to Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite and Draft Diary compiler, Outer Gentleman of Rites and Drafting Gentleman, dispatched over Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初，有盜慈孝寺章獻皇太后神御服器者，既就縶，李絢以屬吏，考掠不得其情，輒釋去。

translations.literal: Initially when thieves stole the sacred vessels of Empress Zhangxian from Cixiao Temple and were seized, Li Xuan entrusted them to subordinate officials; examination under torture did not get the facts and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves stole Empress Zhangxian's sacred vessels from Cixiao Temple and were seized, Li Xuan entrusted them to subordinates; torture did not get facts and they were released.

sentences.zh: 中立至，人復執以來，中立曰：「此真盜也。」

translations.literal: When Zhongli arrived people again brought them; Zhongli said: "This is the true thief."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongli arrived they were brought again; Zhongli said, "This is the true thief."

sentences.zh: 窮治之，卒伏罪。

translations.literal: Investigating to the end they finally confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating to the end they confessed.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: Transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of War, investigating capital punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Outer Gentleman of War, investigating capital punishments.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Made Dragon Diagram Attendant governing Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Made Dragon Diagram Attendant governing Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言者以為非治邊才，改慶州。

translations.literal: Remonstrators said he was not talent for governing the border and changed to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators said he was not border talent and changed him to Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「臣不堪於秦，則不堪於慶矣，願守汝。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your servant is unfit for Qin, then unfit for Qing—I wish to guard Ru."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "I am unfit for Qin, then unfit for Qing—I wish to guard Ru."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply.

sentences.zh: 戍卒有告大校受贓者，中立曰：「是必挾他怨也。」

translations.literal: A garrison soldier reported that a senior commander accepted bribes; Zhongli said: "He surely holds another grievance."
translations.idiomatic: A soldier reported a senior commander accepted bribes; Zhongli said, "He surely holds another grievance."

sentences.zh: 鞭卒竄之。

translations.literal: He flogged the soldier and drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: He flogged the soldier and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「貸奸可乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Can one pardon treachery?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Can one pardon treachery?"

sentences.zh: 中立曰：「部曲得持短長以制其上，則人不自安矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongli said: "If subordinates can hold short and long to control superiors, then people will not be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli said, "If subordinates control superiors by secrets, people will not be at ease."

sentences.zh: 還判太常寺，遷刑部郎中，進樞密直學士、知許州，改陳州。

translations.literal: On return he adjudicated the Grand Temple, transferred to Department Gentleman of Punishments, promoted to Palatial Affairs Attendant governing Xu Prefecture, changed to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he adjudicated the Grand Temple, became Punishments Gentleman, Palatial Affairs Attendant governing Xu, then Chen.

sentences.zh: 訛言大水至，居人皆恐，中立捕誅之。

translations.literal: False rumor said great water was coming; residents were all afraid; Zhongli arrested and executed the spreaders.
translations.idiomatic: False rumor said great water was coming; residents feared; Zhongli arrested and executed spreaders.

sentences.zh: 又徙杭州，暴中風卒。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Hang Prefecture; he suddenly died of wind stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hang Prefecture; he suddenly died of stroke.

sentences.zh: 中立頗以文詞自喜，然嗜酒無行。

translations.literal: Zhongli rather prided himself on literary compositions yet loved wine without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli prided himself on literature yet loved wine without conduct.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，集賢校理蘇舜欽監進奏院，為賽神會，預者皆一時知名士，中立亦在召中。

translations.literal: In Qingli, Collator Su Shunqin supervised the Memorial Transmission Court's spirit-offering gathering—those invited were all famous men of the time; Zhongli was also among those summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli, Collator Su Shunqin supervised the Memorial Transmission Court gathering—all invited were famous; Zhongli was summoned.

sentences.zh: 已而辭不往，後舜欽等得罪，中立有力焉。

translations.literal: He then declined not to go; later when Shunqin and others were punished Zhongli had force in it.
translations.idiomatic: He declined; later when Shunqin and others were punished Zhongli had force in it.

sentences.zh: 沈邈，字子山，信州弋陽人。

translations.literal: Shen Miao, courtesy name Zishan, was a native of Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Miao, whose courtesy name was Zishan, came from Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，起家補大理評事、知侯官縣，通判廣州，累遷都官員外郎，歷知真州、福州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and began as evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Houguan County, vice-prefect of Guang Prefecture, and was repeatedly promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, successively governing Zhen and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, began as Court of Judicial Review evaluator and Houguan magistrate, vice-prefect of Guang, rose to Outer Gentleman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, governing Zhen and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，為侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli he was Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli's first year he was Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時呂夷簡罷相，輔臣皆進官，邈言：「爵祿所以勸臣下，非功而授則為濫。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Yijian was dismissed as chief councillor and assisting ministers all advanced in rank; Miao said: "Rank and salary encourage subordinates—grant without merit and it is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yijian was dismissed assisting ministers advanced; Miao said, "Rank encourages subordinates—grant without merit and it is excessive.

sentences.zh: 今邊鄙屢警，未聞廟堂之謀有以折外侮，無名進秩，臣下何勸焉。」

translations.literal: Now the borders repeatedly alarm yet no plan of the temple is heard to repel outside insult—nameless advancement, how are subordinates encouraged?"
translations.idiomatic: Borders alarm yet no temple plan repels insult—nameless advancement, how are subordinates encouraged?"

sentences.zh: 又論：「夏竦除樞密使，而竦陰交內侍劉從愿。

translations.literal: He also argued: "Xia Song was appointed Bureau Commissioner yet Song secretly associated with inner attendant Liu Congyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He argued, "Xia Song was Bureau Commissioner yet secretly associated with inner attendant Liu Congyuan.

sentences.zh: 使從愿內濟狡譎，竦外專機務，奸黨得計，人主之權去矣。」

translations.literal: Let Congyuan assist treachery within while Song monopolizes affairs without—the treacherous party gains its plan and the ruler's power departs."
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan assists treachery within while Song monopolizes affairs without—traitors gain and the ruler's power departs."

sentences.zh: 其言甚切。

translations.literal: His words were very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: His words were very cutting.

sentences.zh: 權鹽鐵判官，轉兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Acting Salt and Iron adjudicator, transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Salt and Iron adjudicator, transferred to Outer Gentleman of War.

sentences.zh: 時選諸路轉運加按察使，邈與張昷之、王素首被選。

translations.literal: At the time circuit transport commissioners were added as surveillance commissioners; Miao with Zhang Minzhi and Wang Su were first chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit transport commissioners were added as surveillance commissioners; Miao with Zhang Minzhi and Wang Su were first chosen.

sentences.zh: 邈加直史館，使京東。

translations.literal: Miao was added Direct Historian and sent to Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was added Direct Historian and sent to Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered as Attending Censor with supervisory duties.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he entered as Attending Censor with supervisory duties.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢天章閣待制、知澶州，徙河北都轉運使，又徙陝西，歲中，加刑部郎中、知延州，卒。

translations.literal: Before long promoted to Hanlin Attendant of the Heavenly Writings Hall governing Chan Prefecture, transferred to Hebei Circuit Transport Commissioner, again to Shaanxi; within the year added Department Gentleman of Punishments governing Yan Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to Hanlin Attendant governing Chan, Hebei transport, Shaanxi; within the year added Punishments Gentleman governing Yan, and died.

sentences.zh: 邈疏爽有治才，然性少檢。

translations.literal: Miao was open and had governing talent yet his nature was little restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was open and capable yet little restrained.

sentences.zh: 在廣州時，歲遊劉王山，會賓友縱酒，而與閭里婦女，笑言無間。

translations.literal: In Guang Prefecture he yearly toured Mount Liu King, feasted with guests and drank freely, and with neighborhood women laughed and spoke without boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzhou he yearly toured Mount Liu King, feasted and drank freely, and with neighborhood women laughed without boundary.

sentences.zh: 論曰：慶曆以來，任諫官、御史，名有風采，見推於時者，繇臻、京之輩，凡數十人，觀其所陳，蓋不虛得。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Since Qingli, those who held remonstrance and censor posts with reputation and were pushed in the time—from Zhen, Jing, and their generation, several tens of men—viewing what they presented, it was not vainly gained.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion says: Since Qingli, remonstrance and censor officers with reputation pushed in their time—from Zhen, Jing, and their generation, several tens—what they presented was not vainly gained.

sentences.zh: 及之論閹宦，真仁人之言，其最優乎！

translations.literal: Ji's discussion on eunuchs is truly the words of a benevolent man—among them the finest!
translations.idiomatic: Ji's discussion on eunuchs is truly a benevolent man's words—the finest among them!

sentences.zh: 絢、中立、邈亦有美才，致位通顯，然皆以酒失自累，故不能無貶焉。

translations.literal: Xuan, Zhongli, and Miao also had fine talent and reached prominent posts, yet all were burdened by wine faults—therefore they cannot be without demerit.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, Zhongli, and Miao also had fine talent and reached prominence, yet all were burdened by wine faults—therefore they cannot be without demerit.
